raw: Act 2, Scene 5 — Capulet’s Garden
Enter Juliet.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
The clock struck nine when I did send the Nurse,
In half an hour she promised to return.
Perchance she cannot meet him. That’s not so.
O, she is lame. Love’s heralds should be thoughts,
Which ten times faster glides than the sun’s beams,
Driving back shadows over lowering hills:
Therefore do nimble-pinion’d doves draw love,
And therefore hath the wind-swift Cupid wings.
Now is the sun upon the highmost hill
Of this day’s journey, and from nine till twelve
Is three long hours, yet she is not come.
Had she affections and warm youthful blood,
She’d be as swift in motion as a ball;
My words would bandy her to my sweet love,
And his to me.
But old folks, many feign as they were dead;
Unwieldy, slow, heavy and pale as lead.

sentences.en: The clock struck nine when I sent the Nurse.
She promised to return in half an hour.
Maybe she cannot meet him.
No, that is not true.
Oh, she is slow.
Thoughts of love should be the messengers.
They move ten times faster than the sun's rays.
They drive back shadows over low hills.
That is why quick-winged doves pull love's chariot.
And that is why the wind-swift Cupid has wings.
Now the sun is on the highest hill of this day's journey.
From nine until twelve are three long hours.
Yet she has not come.
If she had feelings and warm young blood, she would be as fast as a ball.
My words would carry her to my sweet love.
And his words would come to me.
But many old people act as if they were already dead.
They are clumsy, slow, heavy, and pale like lead.

raw: Enter Nurse and Peter.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
O God, she comes. O honey Nurse, what news?
Hast thou met with him? Send thy man away.

sentences.en: Oh God, she comes.
Oh dear Nurse, what news?
Have you met him?
Send your man away.

speaker: NURSE
raw: Peter, stay at the gate.

sentences.en: Peter, stay at the gate.

raw: Exit Peter.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Now, good sweet Nurse,—O Lord, why look’st thou sad?
Though news be sad, yet tell them merrily;
If good, thou sham’st the music of sweet news
By playing it to me with so sour a face.

sentences.en: Now, good sweet Nurse.
Oh Lord, why do you look sad?
Even if the news is sad, tell it happily.
If it is good news, you ruin the music of the news.
You are playing it to me with such a sour face.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
I am aweary, give me leave awhile;
Fie, how my bones ache! What a jaunt have I had!

sentences.en: I am tired.
Leave me alone for a moment.
Ugh, how my bones ache!
What a long trip I have had!

speaker: JULIET
raw:
I would thou hadst my bones, and I thy news:
Nay come, I pray thee speak; good, good Nurse, speak.

sentences.en: I wish you had my bones and I had your news.
Come on, please speak.
Good, good Nurse, speak.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Jesu, what haste? Can you not stay a while? Do you not see that I am
out of breath?

sentences.en: Jesus, why the hurry?
Can you not stay a while?
Do you not see that I am out of breath?

speaker: JULIET
raw:
How art thou out of breath, when thou hast breath
To say to me that thou art out of breath?
The excuse that thou dost make in this delay
Is longer than the tale thou dost excuse.
Is thy news good or bad? Answer to that;
Say either, and I’ll stay the circumstance.
Let me be satisfied, is’t good or bad?

sentences.en: How are you out of breath?
You have enough breath to tell me that you are out of breath.
The excuse you make for this delay is longer than the story you are telling.
Is your news good or bad?
Answer that question.
Say either, and I will listen to the details.
Let me be satisfied, is it good or bad?

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Well, you have made a simple choice; you know not how to choose a man.
Romeo? No, not he. Though his face be better than any man’s, yet his
leg excels all men’s, and for a hand and a foot, and a body, though
they be not to be talked on, yet they are past compare. He is not the
flower of courtesy, but I’ll warrant him as gentle as a lamb. Go thy
ways, wench, serve God. What, have you dined at home?

sentences.en: Well, you made a foolish choice.
You do not know how to choose a man.
Romeo? No, not him.
His face is better than any man's face.
His leg is better than all men's legs.
His hands and feet are also very good.
They are nothing special to talk about, but still they are the best.
He is not the best at being polite.
But I promise he is as gentle as a lamb.
Go your way, girl, and serve God.
What, did you eat at home?

speaker: JULIET
raw:
No, no. But all this did I know before.
What says he of our marriage? What of that?

sentences.en: No, no.
I knew all of this before.
What does he say about our marriage?
What about that?

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Lord, how my head aches! What a head have I!
It beats as it would fall in twenty pieces.
My back o’ t’other side,—O my back, my back!
Beshrew your heart for sending me about
To catch my death with jauncing up and down.

sentences.en: Lord, how my head aches!
What a head I have!
It feels like it will fall into twenty pieces.
And my back, on the other side!
Oh, my back, my back!
May your heart be cursed for sending me running up and down until I nearly died!

speaker: JULIET
raw:
I’faith, I am sorry that thou art not well.
Sweet, sweet, sweet Nurse, tell me, what says my love?

sentences.en: I am sorry that you are not well.
Sweet, sweet, sweet Nurse, tell me.
What does my love say?

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Your love says like an honest gentleman,
And a courteous, and a kind, and a handsome,
And I warrant a virtuous,—Where is your mother?

sentences.en: Your love speaks like an honest gentleman.
He is courteous and kind.
He is handsome.
I promise he is virtuous.
Where is your mother?

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Where is my mother? Why, she is within.
Where should she be? How oddly thou repliest.
‘Your love says, like an honest gentleman,
‘Where is your mother?’

sentences.en: Where is my mother?
She is inside.
Where else would she be?
You answered very strangely.
'Your love says, like an honest gentleman, where is your mother?'

speaker: NURSE
raw:
O God’s lady dear,
Are you so hot? Marry, come up, I trow.
Is this the poultice for my aching bones?
Henceforward do your messages yourself.

sentences.en: Oh, Holy Mary!
Are you so impatient?
Well, well, calm down!
Is this the cure for my aching bones?
From now on, deliver your messages yourself.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Here’s such a coil. Come, what says Romeo?

sentences.en: This is such a mess.
Come, what does Romeo say?

speaker: NURSE
raw: Have you got leave to go to shrift today?

sentences.en: Do you have permission to go to confession today?

speaker: JULIET
raw: I have.

sentences.en: I have.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Then hie you hence to Friar Lawrence’ cell;
There stays a husband to make you a wife.
Now comes the wanton blood up in your cheeks,
They’ll be in scarlet straight at any news.
Hie you to church. I must another way,
To fetch a ladder by the which your love
Must climb a bird’s nest soon when it is dark.
I am the drudge, and toil in your delight;
But you shall bear the burden soon at night.
Go. I’ll to dinner; hie you to the cell.

sentences.en: Then hurry away to Friar Lawrence's small room.
A husband is waiting there to make you a wife.
Now the excited blood rushes to your cheeks.
They will turn red at any news.
Hurry to the church.
I must go another way.
I must get a ladder.
Your love will use it to climb up to your bird's nest when it is dark.
I am the servant, and I work for your pleasure.
But tonight you will be the one carrying the weight.
Go.
I will go to dinner.
Hurry to the cell.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Hie to high fortune! Honest Nurse, farewell.

sentences.en: Hurry to high fortune!
Honest Nurse, goodbye.

raw: Exeunt.
